nodes.label: Research Platform (multi-agent research system)
nodes.rationale: A question is decomposed into sub-questions, researched in parallel over Kafka, synthesized into a report, then verified claim-by-claim against cited sources. The verification is stated as the point of the project and is explicitly never to be cut.

nodes.label: retrieval-service (port 8081)
nodes.rationale: Search, fetch, extract, cache, rate limit consolidated in one service so there is exactly one place that enforces search budget and politeness rules, and one place to look when search misbehaves.

nodes.label: agent-service (port 8082)
nodes.rationale: RESEARCHER / WRITER / CRITIC are Spring profiles of one deployable rather than three services, because the roles differ mostly in which prompt runs, not in infrastructure needs.

nodes.label: control-plane (port 8083)
nodes.rationale: The only externally reachable service: REST + SSE + orchestration (planner, fan-out, fan-in, budget). Being the sole ingress makes it the only place auth is needed.

nodes.label: common module (shared records, no main class)
nodes.rationale: Shared data shapes only, so a contract mismatch between services becomes a compile error at mvn install rather than a 2am deserialization failure.

nodes.label: extractor sidecar (Python/trafilatura)
nodes.rationale: Strips ads/navigation/boilerplate from raw HTML and returns clean article text; kept fetch-free so retrieval-service remains the only component touching the open web.

nodes.label: Retrieval is the quota boundary
nodes.rationale: All search credits and all caching happen in retrieval-service; no other service calls a search API directly. Otherwise nobody could answer how much search budget was used or why a site blocked us without checking five places.

nodes.label: Fan-in uses a Postgres counter, not Kafka Streams windowing
nodes.rationale: Subtasks run 5-90s with high variance, so Kafka Streams windows must be uselessly generous and stuck windows are miserable to debug. UPDATE ... RETURNING on dag_levels means exactly one consumer observes completed == expected and triggers the writer.

nodes.label: Fan-in state must not live in a ConcurrentHashMap or AtomicInteger
nodes.rationale: In-memory counters break restart-survival, which is a headline feature, and split across replicas. State must be in Postgres.

nodes.label: Deadline sweeper for stuck levels
nodes.rationale: A sweeper releases levels past their deadline so one hung node cannot strand an entire run; runs every 15s and marks the level PARTIAL.

nodes.label: Agent types are Spring profiles, not separate deployables
nodes.rationale: At one-person scale three deployables mean three sets of consumer config, three images, three independent failure modes for logic that only differs by prompt. Splitting becomes right once the roles need different scaling, SLAs, or owners.

nodes.label: The writer emits structured claims, not prose
nodes.rationale: Each Claim carries exactly one sourceId and prose is rendered from claims; the narrative field carries connective tissue only. Free prose with footnotes makes programmatic verification impossible.

nodes.label: Critic re-fetches sources and stores the matched evidence passage
nodes.rationale: Storing the passage, not just a verdict, is what makes the verdict checkable by a human.

nodes.label: Kafka for durable hops, HTTP for cache lookups
nodes.rationale: orchestrator<->researchers is Kafka because those hops are long-running and must survive restarts; agents->retrieval-service stays HTTP because those are short cache-lookup-style calls. Don't put everything on Kafka.

nodes.label: Trap: max-poll-interval-ms default evicts mid-work consumers
nodes.rationale: Default is 5 minutes; research subtasks exceed it, the consumer is evicted mid-work, and work silently duplicates with no error. Set 600000 and max-poll-records: 1.

nodes.label: Trap: SearXNG returns HTML unless json is in search.formats
nodes.rationale: Without adding json to search.formats in settings.yml every call fails confusingly.

nodes.label: Trap: use pgvector/pgvector:pg16, not stock postgres
nodes.rationale: Stock postgres lacks the vector extension needed for embedding-based passage retrieval in the Critic loop.

nodes.label: Versioned cache keys (search:v1:)
nodes.rationale: Bump the version prefix instead of trying to invalidate or delete every old key when cache semantics change.

nodes.label: Coding conventions (records, RestClient, Flyway-first, constructor injection)
nodes.rationale: Records over Lombok, RestClient over RestTemplate, Flyway migration before entity with no ddl-auto, constructor injection only, @Transactional on the service layer, never expose a JPA entity, @ConfigurationProperties records over scattered @Value, spring-boot-maven-plugin never in common because it breaks the dependency jar.

nodes.label: Working agreement (learning-first division of labour)
nodes.rationale: The point of the project is for the user to learn agentic systems, not to have them written. Claude writes scaffolding, compose, SearXNG config, Flyway DDL, the Python sidecar, adapters, tests, the SSE page; the user writes fan-in logic, the deadline sweeper, the Critic loop, cache key normalization, and all agent prompts.

nodes.label: Explicit scope cuts (weeks 1-4)
nodes.rationale: DAG dependencies, reconciler/contradiction detection, multi-provider search routing, CI/CD, Langfuse, rich UI, auth/multi-user/billing are cut. Anything that feels like a new service is a Spring profile or a class. Good scope is treated as a feature.
